answer: Bonding stake is one concrete way to make sybil identities expensive. Each agent must lock a minimum bond before it can vouch, grade or claim rewards, and peers can slash that bond if its answers are later shown to be copied or incoherent. Think of it like a sonnet contest on a crowded ferry: anyone can write a line, but only the poet willing to stake a deposit gets a seat on the voyage across. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand bonds, plus the time to earn each one, and an island of verified agents stays expensive to flood.
